latency_ms_p50.note: not comparable across families: the competitor figures are pool retrieval only (in-memory), nanomem's is a full Vault.search including its ranking layer against an on-disk vault.

findings.note: Every value here is read back out of this file's own `arms` block; nothing is hand-entered.

floor_is_the_storage_format_not_the_laye.claim: fp16-on-disk costs nothing on this set: nanomem with every entity/temporal addition zeroed is bit-identical in ranking to exhaustive fp32 cosine, so every nanomem delta below is the ranking layer.

supersession_is_real.claim: a plain vector store really does return the superseded value: on current-value questions the exact-cosine floor answers with an OLDER revision this often.

shipped_default_has_no_net_benefit.claim: at shipped defaults (temporal_direction left alone, which is what chat.py and cli.py do -- neither ever sets it) nanomem is not better than no temporal logic at all overall, and is much worse on historical questions.

competitor_heuristic_wins.claim: a ~20-line recency heuristic on top of Chroma or sqlite-vec beats nanomem's entity layer on this benchmark.

adjacent_attribute_regression.claim: USER_MANUAL_DEVELOPER.md ('Temporal revisions') states that 40 of 40 adjacent-but-different attributes are left alone, the same as plain cosine, citing ranking_dev_r4_shipped.json. On this fixture-free set that does not reproduce: the layer merges siblings and answers with the wrong one.

third_party_leak.claim: entities.py documents that a third party's attribute cannot be returned for 'what is MY ...' (third_party_v3r4.json). The reverse leak is not covered: an INNER possessive that also carries a first-person marker ('my colleague X's desk phone') is tagged per-possessor on the record side, but query_intent drops the possessor on the query side, so the user's own value wins.

nobody_answers_previous_value.claim: 'the value just before the current one' is unsolved by every two-way arm, including both oracles, because both nanomem's shipped historical_mode and the competitor heuristic return the OLDEST. The *_3way arms show what the fix is worth.

oracle_vs_oracle.claim: given the SAME gift -- a perfect write-time attribute extractor -- Chroma plus recency beats nanomem plus metadata['entity'].

chroma_recency.note: delta and pool size were swept ON THE TEST SET and the value that maximises the COMPETITOR's top-1 was kept. That is an optimistic upper bound in the competitor's favour; nanomem got no equivalent tuning.

sqlite_recency.note: delta and pool size were swept ON THE TEST SET and the value that maximises the COMPETITOR's top-1 was kept. That is an optimistic upper bound in the competitor's favour; nanomem got no equivalent tuning.

pairwise.note: paired bootstrap over questions, 10,000 resamples. Questions within a user are not independent, so these intervals are optimistic; the user-level n is only 10.

holdout.note: Competitor delta/pool tuned on users u01, u02 ONLY; every arm is then scored on the remaining 8 users. This removes the tuned-on-test advantage the headline table hands the competitors.

arm.description: exhaustive float32 cosine over the same vectors, no temporal logic whatsoever. The floor.
chromadb EphemeralClient, cosine space, precomputed shared embeddings, top-k as returned.
sqlite-vec vec0 KNN in an in-memory database, top-k as returned.

the twenty-line heuristic a competent engineer writes: infer direction from wording, treat candidates within delta cosine of the best as one fact, order that group by timestamp. kpool=3 delta=0.080 (swept, best-for-competitor)
the same heuristic with delta and pool size chosen on the two DEV users only (kpool=3 delta=0.060); the holdout table is the clean comparison.

ORACLE, not a product: Chroma plus a PERFECT write-time attribute extractor. The true (subject, attribute) group of the best candidate is ordered by timestamp. Ceiling for any competitor that runs an LLM tagger on ingest.
ABSOLUTE CEILING: additionally handed the question's own true (subject, attribute) and true direction. Nothing deployable can reach this; it measures the recency rule alone.
CONTROL, not a shipped configuration: nanomem with every entity and temporal addition zeroed. Isolates the fp16-on-disk storage format from the ranking layer -- it should equal exact_cosine_floor.
nanomem 0.3.0 shipped defaults, reopened vault, temporal_direction left at its default 'current'.
nanomem with temporal_direction taken from the SAME wording classifier the Chroma and sqlite-vec arms use.
nanomem handed the question's true direction. Oracle arm.

ORACLE MIRROR of chroma_oracle_group: every fact written with the documented metadata['entity'] tag (USER_MANUAL_DEVELOPER.md, 'Temporal revisions'), i.e. a perfect write-time extractor, plus the wording direction. Group labels are the benchmark's own attribute names.
nanomem with a three-way wording direction, flipping engine.historical_mode to 'previous' for 'just before this one' questions. Same upgrade given to chroma_recency_3way.

the same perfect extractor, but with the group labels expressed in nanomem's own vocabulary (entities.query_intent), so its intent hoist can fire. See aligned_entity_map(). This is nanomem's best possible arm on this benchmark.
